title: Launch Orbit Manifest - Night & Day Handoff + Release Notes Draft
body:
Goal and scope:
A compact, ops-friendly manifest for the Nov-2026 launch window. Primary goal: ensure smooth 48-hour stabilization after feature flip with clear human handoffs, prioritized telemetry checks, and a user-facing release notes draft that can be shipped within 2 hours of go-live if needed. Scope: region staggered flip (us-west -> us-east -> eu-west), backend changes (kv-cache rekey + batching optimization), fallback model-routing enabled.

High-level launch plan (summary):
- T-72h: freeze non-critical merges, final smoke branch cut, smoke test pass required.
- T-24h: dry-run with synthetic traffic on staging and limited canary on dedicated pool.
- T-2h: preflight (see preflight matrix).
- T+0: staggered flip sequence — us-west 10:00 PT, us-east +30m, eu-west +90m.
- T+0 to T+48h: stabilization and telemetry-driven throttles; emergency rollback window first 2 hours per-region.

Night & day handoff choreography (explicit):
- Primary owners: Day shift (10:00 PT - 22:00 PT): Priya (launch lead), Ethan (telemetry), Lina (oncall escalation).
- Night shift (22:00 PT - 10:00 PT): Daniel (night conductor), Maya (release eng backup).
- Handoff protocol: 15-minute async summary message to #launch-orbit in Slack with: current region, last observed 5m p50/p95 latency, token cost delta, top 3 alerts (severity >= P3). Use template: "HANDOFF: region=us-east, window=T+4h, p95=210ms (+22ms), errors=1.2% (rate spike), actions=rate-limit-2."
- If a P1 is active, no handoff until resolved or formally reassigned.

Preflight micro-check matrix (T-2h):
- Smoke end-to-end generation (fast path): PASS
- KV cache warmup (sample prefix queries): PASS
- Batching stress (500 concurrent small reqs): PASS
- Auth and rate-limit sanity: PASS
- Canary fallback routing test (simulate GPU OOM): PASS
- Telemetry dashboard health (all widgets load <3s): PASS
Unresolved: synthetic KV warmup sometimes returns cache-miss spikes in region-b — plan: run warmup with replica-binding to avoid cold cache.

Region flip cadence details (stagger):
1) us-west: flip traffic weight from 0->100% over 10m with 10% steps, hold 15m between steps.
2) us-east: start 30m after us-west initial step; follow same stepping.
3) eu-west: start 90m after us-west.
Fail-fast rules: if error rate increases >0.8% absolute or p95 increases >40% for two consecutive 5-minute windows, pause traffic and roll back region to previous model variant.

Telemetry checklist (quick) - queries to run on failure or anomaly:
- 5m p50/p95 request latency per-region per-model: QUERY_ID=QT-LAT-001
- 5m request error-rate (>=500/4xx/429) per-route: QUERY_ID=QT-ERR-002
- Token cost vs baseline (24h prior) per-model: QT-COST-003
- KV cache hit ratio per-keyspace: QT-KV-004
- GPU mem alloc and OOM events: QT-HOST-005
- Long-tail token generation time (95-99 pctile for long prompts): QT-LONG-006
Notes: Ethan will paste the concrete Grafana panels during T-1h in the Slack thread. If any QT-* shows delta > threshold, initiate mitigation path.

Mitigation ladder (prescriptive):
1) Toggle conservative batcher (reduce max_batch_size from 64->32) — roll via feature-flag -> expected immediate latency improvement but higher token cost.
2) Mobility routing: route 10% to fallback smaller model variant for 20m to test quality degrade.
3) Scale-up reserved pool by +1 GPU node (requires Dedicated ops approval) — expected time to effect 6-8 min.
4) Rollback region to previous model variant (documented rollback PR).

Communications snippets (for Slack/cs/exec):
- Short alert for SRE/Oncall: "ALERT: us-west p95 340ms (+80ms). Pausing next step and invoking batcher toggle. See thread #launch-orbit."
- Customer-facing line for CS: "We deployed performance improvements to generation routing; a small subset of customers may see transient latency changes — we are monitoring and will update within 30m."
- Exec short: "Launch Orbit: us-west paused at T+12m due to p95 delta; mitigation in progress (batching toggle)."

Release notes (user-facing draft) — short form (to be copy-edited by product writing):
Title: Performance and routing updates to reduce inference cost
What changed:
- Improved request routing to reduce median token cost for short prompts by ~12% (rolling improvement across regions).
- Server-side batching optimizations to improve throughput under bursty workloads.
- Fallback routing now enabled to keep requests served during high mem pressure.

Why this matters:
- Lower per-request cost and improved stability during traffic spikes. Some very long prompts may experience slightly higher tail latency during ramp; we are monitoring and will revert if user impact observed.
Known issues:
- In rare cases with very long context (>16k tokens) generation p95 can increase by ~10-15% while cache warms. Workaround: resubmit with trimmed context or request smaller max_tokens.

Release notes (internal annotations):
- performance numbers are preliminary; do not publish exact cost-savings per-customer until QA metrics validated (eta T+24h).
- Link to regression eval: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/REL/Launch-Orbit-Evals

Post-release 0-48h forensic tasks (owners and timing):
- 0-2h: burn-in checks every 15m (Ethan): latency, errors, kv hit ratio, GPU OOMs. Log anomalies to incident sheet.
- 2-8h: medium analysis (Priya): compare 1h windows vs 24h baseline; check customer-affecting routes.
- 8-24h: quality evals (Lina/Maya): run eval prompts for regression, summarize at 24h.
- 24-48h: cost reconciliation draft (Daniel): preliminary unit-cost delta and recommendation for batcher default.

Runbook snippets & quick commands (copyable):
- Toggle conservative batcher: curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.com/feature-flag/toggle -d '{"flag":"conservative_batcher","value":true}' (ops token required)
- Re-route 10% to fallback: ./scripts/reroute-traffic.sh --region us-west --percent 10 --variant fallback-v2
- Grafana perf panel: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/launch-orbit/perf

Open questions / decision points to resolve before go: (marked "[ACTION]")
- [ACTION] Confirm Dedicated ops approval path for emergency scale-up (+1 GPU) — Daniel to confirm by T-12h.
- [ACTION] Finalize acceptable tail-latency threshold per-region (proposal: p95 <= 350ms) — Prod/Perf to sign-off.
- [ACTION] Decide whether to include explicit customer opt-out for fallback routing (privacy/reg implications) — Legal/Product to advise.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep the Slack thread tidy; pin the key Grafana panels.
- If we see correlated increase in 4xx errors, check auth token refresh window (recent change in oidc lib).
- Remember to attach the final release notes draft to customer digest channel and to the release checklist page in Confluence.

Appendix: quick checklist (checkbox-style)
- [ ] Merge smoke branch and tag release
- [ ] Copy release notes draft into product writer doc
- [ ] Preflight matrix all PASS
- [ ] Warm KV caches in region order
- [ ] Notify CS with customer-facing FAQ
- [ ] Oncall roster confirmed for 48h

End of manifest.

-- Maya K. (release engineering)
